shared_elements: low relief carved in pale stone
quadruped animal shown in profile facing right
animal heads with rendered eye and muzzle
horizontal band or register of repeated pattern
justification: Both are pale stone reliefs whose main motif is a quadruped in strict profile facing right, and both use a horizontal band of repeated pattern above the figural zone as an organising device. Beyond that they diverge sharply: A is a smoothly finished single-register procession with anatomically detailed animals, patterned fleece and accompanying human figures, while B is a roughly dressed upright pillar with schematic, flattened, vertically stacked creatures and no human presence.
